# Independent audit: global cap baseline and one-fiber canonical escape


candidate 9040ddab36f28107,
independently differentiated the mixed physical/threshold terms,
checked the exact completion of squares, and ran its standard-library
verifier. No mathematical repair is needed.

The result concerns the stated one-fiber physical variation and one
selected concurrent group. The source retains the actual cap curvature
of every unchanged fiber. It makes no claim about discarded group
budgets or arbitrary inclusion-minimal cap covers.

## 1. Exact baseline, first stress, and quadratic equivalence

The identity

    c_i(W,theta)=F_i(W,theta)-F_i(I,theta)+G_i(theta)-G_i(0)

is exact. The selected-fiber subtraction cancels its pure theta
derivatives inside that difference, but the complete original-source
baseline G remains. Thus the pure parameter term in the Hessian
must be D²G, exactly as displayed.

The physical map f_i(B)=V Gamma (tr B+row_i B) is onto; the
specified right inverse has zero column sums. Its trace satisfies
V tr R(f)=sum f_i/(m Gamma). Hence ell_i=1/(m Gamma) has the
correct absolute-volume normalization.

If ell.DG is nonzero, the signed parameter direction and the
physical compensation -R(DG) have zero individual cap derivatives
and strictly positive mass derivative. The IFT and smaller strict
cap correction are valid in the explicitly assumed open
compatibility neighborhood.

If ell.DG=0, the stated critical equations force zero volume first
derivative. I checked the exact Hessian (7), including its factor
two on the mixed block. Adding acceleration R(-q-xi 1) changes
each cap second derivative to -xi and the volume second derivative
to Q-xi/Gamma. With xi=Gamma Q/2 these are -Gamma Q/2 and Q/2.
Conversely, objective-one stationarity and positive ell make the
same identity necessary for a strict second-order escape. The
qualification excluding higher-order zero-Hessian paths is correct.

The C2 hypothesis is needed and explicitly stated. It is not
deduced merely from proper polytope sections.

## 2. Coarea sign and parameter accelerations

For margin L=u.x-b and velocity w, differentiation of the
halfspace indicator gives delta(L)w at first order and
delta(L)kappa+delta'(L)w² at second order. Integrating the latter
term by the fixed-normal coarea coordinate gives the negative
section derivative in (9), with factor 1/|u|. The displayed sign
is correct. Variation of the normal is included in w(x); the
chart's second margin derivative kappa is not discarded.

As the source notes, existence of that weighted section derivative
and the needed C2 regularity must be supplied before using this
formula. It is not an unconditional formula at a supporting
facet or a combinatorial singularity.

## 3. The whole homothetic baseline

After normalizing the selected radius to one, the canonical
one-vertex cap on r_z K has volume

    V (r_z h-tau_i)^d.

Because the support is finite and all radii are positive, there is
one neighborhood where every such cut is proper with the same
one-positive-vertex pattern. The full baseline is therefore (11)
and is analytic there.

Its derivatives are

    -V m Gamma S v_i,
    V Gamma m²(d-1) N_2 v_i²/d.

I checked the powers of r_z and the d=2 convention N_2=|P|.
Summing the critical cap equations gives tr B=0; the remaining
equations give row B=mS v. Thus the first stress holds but the
baseline curvature does not vanish.

For completeness, direct differentiation of the selected proper-cap
formula yields the mixed derivative

    D_tau D_W F_i[B,v]
       =V Gamma [-m(tr B+row_i B)+(m²/d)B_ii]v_i.

Multiplication by the Lagrange multipliers and the mixed factor two
gives exactly 2r.v-2m b.v/d in (15), with sum v_i=0.
This independently checks its sign and normalization.

## 4. Optimization over every physical critical velocity

For fixed diagonal b and row vector r, the displayed A_min has
row sums r-b and column sums -b. Its entries are additive in the
row and column labels, so it is orthogonal to every off-diagonal
perturbation with zero row and column sums. Its squared norm in
(17) follows by expansion. The decomposition A=A_min+Z therefore
includes every physical critical velocity, not just a special
ansatz.

Substituting r=mS v into (14)--(17) gives the completed square

    Q/V = m(d-1)Theta ||v||²/d
          -||b-[d²S-m(d-1)]v||²/[d(d-1)]
          -||Z||²/m,
    Theta=d(S-1)²+1-N_2.

The maximizing matrix (20) has zero column sums and trace and
the required row sums. I independently checked these identities.
For Theta>0 any nonzero sum-zero v yields a positive direction;
for Theta<=0 every critical direction has nonpositive Hessian.
This proves the stated necessary-and-sufficient strict quadratic
criterion in the specified parameter space.

For two radii 1,t, Theta=t^(d-2)(d t^d-1). If t^d<1/d, the
completed square is negative definite on the entire critical
tangent: equality would require v=0, b=0, and Z=0, hence B=0.
Surjectivity and the positive multipliers justify the stated strict
local maximum under cap inequalities in this restricted chart.
No normal-rotation or multifiber conclusion follows, and none is
claimed.

The unnormalized condition (24) has the correct factor r_p^d.

## 5. Smallest-radius positivity and actual strictification

If the selected radius is minimal, all normalized other radii are
at least one. Write A=sum_(z!=p) r_z^(d-1)>0 and
B=sum_(z!=p) r_z^(d-2). The inequalities in the source give
B<=A², including d=2. Consequently Theta=dA²-B>0 for d>=2.
The identical-fiber specializations and the planar value Q/V=18
at three fibers and v=(1,-1,0) follow exactly.

The referenced radial-layer barrier applies because the affine
centroid section is interior to every positive homothetic simplex.
It preserves total mass and all initial canonical budgets
Gamma M exactly, and supplies a uniform excluded-self support
gap. Selfweights and lattice completeness are handled by that
proved dependency.

The original smallest fiber need not remain smallest after the
preliminary step; continuity of its strictly positive Theta is
enough, as the source correctly uses. Renormalize by the current
selected radius when applying the formulas. Its current volume
is the V in the absolute right inverse and Hessian.

All homothetic cap functions are analytic in the positive radii,
physical simplex parameters, and the common proper threshold
chamber. The explicit acceleration therefore yields the stated
strict second-order cap decreases and mass increase. Taking the
physical motion sufficiently small after fixing the strictification
preserves actual compatibility. The group remains a whole-space
cover because its margins continue to sum to zero.

Only one physical fiber moves in that last stage. The other
fibers' actual curvature remains the N_2 term; it has not been
replaced by parameter flatness.

## 6. Exact verification and limitations

The command

    python3 supporting computation verify_global_cap_baseline_curvature_and_one_fiber_escape.py

passes all 133 exact checks. Its independent second-order series
expansion includes every unchanged homothetic fiber. It checks
the completion of squares, the critical constraints, the physical
acceleration, and an exact rational three-fiber planar path.
The finite path's barycentric containment matrix is strictly
positive, so its actual compatibility is checked as sets, not
only through scalar volume concavity.

The all-dimensional conclusion rests on the exact formulas and
the proved radial barrier, not on the finite dimension range in
the verifier. The theorem retains one group only. Shared
originals or additional groups must impose their own coupled
coefficient identities and actual budget derivatives before this
mode can be reused.

## 7. Added equal-canonical-fraction rigidity

The subsequently added Section 6 also **PASSES**. I read its
dependency candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c
and checked the new orientation/homothety step.

If a fiber centroid g has l_i(g)>0, the through-g cap is a strict
subcap of its fraction-Gamma through-section cap: a slab near
the interior point g has positive volume. Ordinary Grunbaum
contradicts that strict decrease. Thus every l_i(g)<=0. Their
sum is zero and they span the continuous dual space, forcing
g to equal the section point.

The selected whole-space cover bounds every point's ordinary
depth by Gamma. The archived ordinary rigidity theorem then
makes the fiber a simplex. Its single-cap equality case has
the required apex-side orientation. In a simplex the apex is
one vertex and the base consists of the opposite facet, so the
selected normal identifies that facet's barycentric gradient
with a positive scale.

The original canonical circuit has d+1 distinct directions and
one-dimensional dependence space. Matching all d+1 facets and
summing the new barycentric gradients therefore forces their
positive scales to coincide. Because the already proved centroid
is the section point, their constant terms are all 1/(d+1).
This gives exactly the common positive homothety in equation (25).

The result requires the exact canonical fractions Gamma and the
same through-section group in every fiber. It does not classify
arbitrary equal fraction vectors or noncanonical cap tuples.
